description: Sync issues and pull requests, each with its whole discussion, from the GitHub repositories you choose.
intro: The GitHub connector reads the repositories you select. Each issue and each pull request becomes one document that carries its body and its whole discussion: conversation comments and, for a pull request, review comments and review summaries.
Issues and pull requests are linked to the issues they reference or close, to their parent issue, and to the Linear issues, Slack messages and Notion pages they link to.

connect.auth: GitHub uses a personal access token. A classic token needs `repo`, or `public_repo` for public repositories only. A fine-grained token works with the access GitHub grants it.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A GitHub personal access token with read access to repositories and issues.

permissions.name: public_repo
permissions.text: public repositories only. Use this or `repo`.

permissions.name: repo
permissions.text: private and public repositories. Reading a private repository's collaborators for permissions also needs it.

permissions.name: read:org
permissions.text: reads which organization teams can access a repository, for permissions. If GitHub refuses it, the connector raises a permission warning.

connect.permissions_note: HydraDB checks for `repo` or `public_repo` only when GitHub reports the token's scopes. Fine-grained tokens may not report them.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: In GitHub, create a personal access token with `repo`, or `public_repo` for public repositories only. Add `read:org` if you want organization team access captured.

steps.title: Select repositories
steps.text: Discover lists every repository the token's user owns, collaborates on, or can see as an organization member. Select the repositories to sync.

connect.account: GitHub rate limits apply per token, so a large first sync can use up the hourly quota. That is why the first sync is bounded.

documents.name: Issues and pull requests
documents.one_document: One issue or one pull request, with its whole discussion inside it.
documents.title: The issue or pull request title.
documents.text: The body. Each comment, review comment and review summary is added as its own searchable part of the item, with its author and time, and for a review comment the file, line and the comment it replies to. Empty comments are skipped. Labels are written as a `Labels` line, the creation time as a `Created` line, and a sub-issue's parent as a `Parent` line.
documents.date: When the issue or pull request was last updated.
documents.link_back: The issue or pull request page on GitHub.
documents.files: Images and files in bodies and comments are not downloaded.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: Names the result. HydraDB also scans it for Linear issue keys and links.

attributes.name: body
attributes.text: The main text. References in it become links: `#123`, `owner/repo#123`, closing keywords, and Linear, Slack and Notion links.

attributes.name: Comments
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: Each comment, review comment and review summary is searchable with the item. Its author is recorded as a commenter, and references inside it become links of the item.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.text: Written as the `Labels` line, so a query can match a label.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: Written as the `Created` line.

attributes.name: Item id
attributes.text: The id `owner/repo#number`. It keeps later syncs on the same document, and it is what items in other tools, such as Linear issues, link to.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the item was last updated. It is the document date, and it moves with every edit or new comment.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.github_repo
attributes.text: The repository as `owner/name`. Limits a query to one repository.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.github_issue_number
attributes.text: The issue or pull request number. Targets one item.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `github`.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: A sub-issue's parent issue, as `owner/repo#number`. Links the sub-issue to its parent, and is written as the `Parent` line.

attributes.name: is_pr
attributes.text: Marks a pull request, so closing keywords in its body link it to the issues it closes.

attributes.name: mentions
purposes: Person or group in the graph
attributes.text: Each `@username` in the body, recorded as a person the item mentions.

attributes.name: Repository
attributes.text: The selected repository. Its audience decides who can read every issue and pull request in it.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The login of the person who opened the item. It is not searchable and not added to the graph as a person.

attributes.name: assignees
attributes.text: Assignee logins. Not searchable, and not added to the graph.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: `open` or `closed`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: closed_at
attributes.text: When the item was closed.

attributes.name: milestone, milestone_due
attributes.text: The milestone title and its due date.

connections: A sub-issue to its parent issue.
An issue or pull request to each issue or pull request it references in its body or discussion.
A pull request to each issue its body closes with a closing keyword.
An issue or pull request to a Linear issue it links to, or names after a closing word.
An issue or pull request to a Slack message or Notion page it links to.
In the other direction, Linear issues link to the GitHub pull requests attached to them.
References inside code blocks, inline code and HTML comments are ignored.
people: The author of each comment, as a commenter.
The person who opened the item and its assignees are not declared as people.
graph.from_text: The body and discussion text: topics, decisions, and people and projects named in prose.

permissions.who_can_read: Access follows the repository, not the single issue. A public or internal repository can be read by everyone in your HydraDB tenant unless you set an access rule. A private repository can be read by its collaborators and by the organization teams that have access to it.
permissions.identity: The email address on a collaborator's public GitHub profile. Teams are added as groups.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a collaborator hides their profile email, the collaborator list is incomplete, there are too many people to express, or GitHub refuses a request, the connector raises a permission warning. An access rule you set on the repository stays in force. Without a rule, depending on your deployment's setting, the repository's items are either readable by everyone or hidden until permissions can be read.
notes: One collaborator with a hidden public email stops HydraDB from capturing a private repository's audience. Set an access rule on such a repository.
Internal repositories are open to everyone in your HydraDB tenant. Check that this matches who should see them.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back 30 days by default, set by `lookback_days`. The window is measured from the repository's most recent activity, not from today, so a quiet repository still brings in its last stretch of work.
sync.changes: Each sync asks GitHub for items updated since the last sync. A changed item is sent again with its whole discussion.
sync.edits: Editing an issue or pull request, or adding a comment, moves its updated time, so the whole item is sent again.
sync.deletes: Deleted issues and pull requests are not removed. An item that disappears from GitHub can stay searchable in HydraDB.

not_synced: Releases, wikis, projects and GitHub Discussions.
Images and files attached in bodies and comments.
Repositories the token's user cannot see.
questions: What was decided in the discussion on the pull request that added rate limiting?
Which issues in `acme/api` are labelled bug and mention the login timeout?
Which Linear issue does this pull request close?
What did reviewers say about the caching change in `acme/web`?

good_to_know.title: Who opened or owns an item is not searchable.
good_to_know.text: The opener, the assignees and whether the item is open are stored on it, but a query does not match them.

good_to_know.title: Comments arrive inside their issue or pull request.
good_to_know.text: Each comment is part of its issue or pull request, so a result is the whole item, not a single comment.
